newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine winter crop in good shape, still at risk.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine winter crop in good shape, still at risk.

text.p: Ukraine's all-important winter grain crop is weathering the cold better than it did last year, but the risk of damage still exists, Agriculture Science Academy deputy chairman Volodymyr Krut said on Monday.
"Winter grain has suffered only minor damage this season, and far less than at this time last year," he said in an interview.
"I do see a future risk, because the possibility of a drop in temperatures in areas without snow cover still exists."
Much of the wheat grown in Ukraine, a former breadbasket of the Soviet Union, is of the winter variety, and is planted in autumn to sit through the winter for harvesting the next year.
Winter grain grows best when it has thick snows to keep protected from damaging frosts.
According to the Agriculture Ministry, 7.44 million hectares were sown to winter wheat out of a total of 8.24 million sown to winter grain late last year, compared to 7.89 million hectares in 1995.
Government plans for sowing 8.61 million hectares with winter grain fell short due to a lack of machinery and fuel.
Krut forecast a far smaller resowing campaign this spring, after Ukraine's farmers last year resowed up to 600,000 hectares with spring grain to make up for crops lost to winterkill.

Anatoly Prokopenko, a deputy head of the State Weather Forecasting Center, said fields in the central and northern parts of the country were without thick snow cover, raising concerns about the winter grain's future.
"As of today there is no grain damage, but we are expecting small snowfalls and sub-zero temperatures all around Ukraine," he said.

Prokopenko said that snowcover in western and southern Ukraine ranged from one to 30 cm, and temperatures ranged from minus 1.0 - minus 7.0 Celsius during the day to minus 10 - minus 12 Celsius at night.
Last year's total grain harvest, one of the worst on record for the country, fell to 25.4 million tonnes compared to 36.5 million tonnes in 1995.
Of that total, Ukraine harvested only 13.4 million tonnes of winter wheat, down from 16.4 million tonnes in 1995.
Officials said the government wanted to raise the total 1997 grain harvest to 38 million tonnes and that farmers planned to use more fertilisers to increase crop yields.
